pages.text: Their teacher took the class on an animal walk around the school compound. “Look, listen, and write,” she said. “Do not touch any animal. We only watch.” Oppong and Naab drew a neat table with four headings: insects, birds, mammals, and reptiles.
sentences: Their teacher took the class on an animal walk around the school compound.
“Look, listen, and write,” she said.
“Do not touch any animal.
We only watch.” Oppong and Naab drew a neat table with four headings: insects, birds, mammals, and reptiles.
pages.alt: Oppong, Naab, and their Ghanaian teacher in a green patterned dress walk carefully around a sunlit school compound holding plain open notebooks.

pages.text: On a green leaf, Naab spotted a grasshopper. “It has six legs, and its body has three parts,” she said. “Those are signs of an insect.” Nearby, ants carried crumbs and a butterfly landed on a flower. They wrote all three under insects.
sentences: On a green leaf, Naab spotted a grasshopper.
“It has six legs, and its body has three parts,” she said.
“Those are signs of an insect.” Nearby, ants carried crumbs and a butterfly landed on a flower.
They wrote all three under insects.
pages.alt: Oppong and Naab crouch safely beside a bush watching a green grasshopper on a leaf, trailing ants, and a colourful butterfly on a flower.

pages.text: A speckled hen scratched in the dust, and a small weaver bird sat on the classroom roof. “Birds have feathers, wings, a beak, and two legs,” said Oppong. “And they lay eggs.” They wrote hen and bird under birds.
sentences: A speckled hen scratched in the dust, and a small weaver bird sat on the classroom roof.
“Birds have feathers, wings, a beak, and two legs,” said Oppong.
“And they lay eggs.” They wrote hen and bird under birds.
pages.alt: A speckled brown hen scratches in the dusty schoolyard while a yellow weaver bird perches on the classroom roof as Oppong and Naab watch.

pages.text: By the wooden fence stood a brown goat, and a dog slept in the shade. “Mammals have hair or fur,” said the teacher. “A mother mammal feeds her babies with milk.” Naab giggled. “People are mammals, too!”
sentences: By the wooden fence stood a brown goat, and a dog slept in the shade.
“Mammals have hair or fur,” said the teacher.
“A mother mammal feeds her babies with milk.” Naab giggled.
“People are mammals, too!”
pages.alt: A brown goat stands near a wooden school fence beside a sleeping dog in the shade while the teacher talks warmly with Oppong and Naab.

pages.text: On a warm wall, an agama lizard lay still in the sun. “Reptiles have dry skin covered with scales,” said Oppong. “Many lay eggs on land, and they warm up in the sun.” A green frog hopped past on the damp grass. “Its skin is wet and smooth,” said Naab. “It does not belong to any of our four groups.”
sentences: On a warm wall, an agama lizard lay still in the sun.
“Reptiles have dry skin covered with scales,” said Oppong.
“Many lay eggs on land, and they warm up in the sun.” A green frog hopped past on the damp grass.
“Its skin is wet and smooth,” said Naab.
“It does not belong to any of our four groups.”
pages.alt: An agama lizard basks on a sunny compound wall while a smooth green frog hops across damp grass nearby as Oppong and Naab observe.

pages.text: Back in class, the teacher smiled. “The frog belongs to another group called amphibians, which we will study later,” she said. “Every animal moves, feeds, and reproduces to have young. Which of these life processes did you see today?” The class named them proudly and cheered.

pages.alt: Inside the bright Ghanaian classroom, the teacher stands beside a wordless four-column picture chart of animal drawings while Oppong, Naab, and classmates cheer.

activities.question: How many legs does an insect have?
Which animals feed their babies with milk?

activities.definition: An animal with dry skin covered in scales.

glossary.definition: A small animal with six legs and a body in three parts.
Animals with hair or fur whose mothers feed their babies milk.
Small, hard, thin plates that cover the skin of reptiles.
